title: Adaptive Priority Routing Patterns for Degraded Inference Modes
body:
Summary:
This note proposes an adaptive "priority lanes" routing pattern for graceful degradation across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments. The goal is to keep customer-facing applications online during capacity constraints or region failures while preserving predictable latency and cost signals. This pattern supplements existing tiered capacity and model-variant fallbacks with a lightweight control-plane policy that classifies requests into lanes and drives routing, batching, and cache decisions accordingly.

Why a new pattern?
- Existing approaches focus on binary fallback or regional spillover. We observed gaps when mixed workloads (low-latency chat + heavy batch embedding jobs) compete for the same pool: suboptimal latency for high-priority requests and opaque cost increases.
- Priority lanes provide a compact, auditable policy surface for SREs, product owners, and customer success to tune behavior without ad-hoc rules per service.

Core concepts:
1) Lanes: labeled request classes (gold, silver, bronze, background). Labels applied by API key tier, route config, or incoming headers.
2) Model Variant Chain: for each lane define an ordered list of model variants to try (e.g., r-instruct-xl -> r-instruct-xl-quantized -> r-distilled-small).
3) Capacity Pools & Overflow Matrix: physical pools scoped by region and capability (low-latency GPUs, cost-optimized TPUs, CPU-quantized nodes). A prioritized spillover matrix defines where to send excess load by lane.
4) Soft Degradation: attempts to degrade along model variant chain before region-level spillover; preserves quality as long as possible.
5) Cache & Prefix Priority: prefix cache entries can be lane-aware to favor gold lane cache hits.

Policy language (pseudo):
- route.rules = [
    {lane: "gold", retry: 0, model_chain: ["r-xl", "r-xl-q8"], max_latency_ms: 120},
    {lane: "silver", retry: 1, model_chain: ["r-xl-q8", "r-medium"], max_latency_ms: 250},
    {lane: "bronze", retry: 2, model_chain: ["r-medium", "r-small"], max_latency_ms: 800}
  ]
- spillover.matrix[regionA][lane] = [regionA:local, regionB:low-cost, regionC:dedicated-burst]

Control plane responsibilities:
- Centralized policy store: versioned policies per customer/route with canary staging and rollout.
- Real-time capacity view: aggregate tokens/sec, active sessions, queued requests per pool.
- Decision API: given request metadata (lane, region preference, SLO tags) return target pool and model variant. Decisions are idempotent and fast (<2ms).
- Telemetry: emit decision reason codes (LOCAL_OK, MODEL_DEGRADATION, REGION_SPILLOVER, RATE_LIMITED) and attach to traces.

Operational flow (happy path -> constrained):
1) Request classified to lane at ingress.
2) Control plane queries pool state and returns preferred pool + model variant.
3) Runtime attempts local execution with continuous batching. If model variant not available, fallthrough to next variant (soft degrade).
4) If local pools are saturated beyond configured thresholds, runtime consults spillover matrix and routes to remote pool.
5) If remote pool rejects (policy or capacity), enforce lane-level rate limiting or backpressure.

Metrics to track (per lane + global):
- p50/p95 generation latency
- per-token cost estimate
- model-variant usage fraction
- cache hit ratio (prefix + KV) by lane
- spillover events per minute and downstream latency delta
- quality regression score: anchored eval set trigger failures after variant switch

Rollback & safety knobs:
- Per-customer global kill switch (route->degrade_to_read_only)
- Canary policy rollouts: percent of requests by origin region and lane
- Auto-revert if quality-regression hits threshold (e.g., eval loss increase or user-facing error spikes)

Simulation plan (short):
- Build a synthetic mixed-workload generator: 60% chat (gold/silver), 30% embeddings (bronze/background), 10% batch fine-tune.
- Run regional outage scenarios and 2x load spikes. Track latency, cost per token, and failed requests.
- Gate: policy must keep gold p95 <150ms for 99% of simulated core-user traffic.

Example incident playbook (concise):
- Detection: spike in REGION_SPILLOVER telemetry or degraded gold p95 >= threshold.
- Triage: platform on-call checks control plane capacity view and recent policy changes.
- Mitigation: 1) enable additional spillover targets for gold lane, 2) temporarily increase gold SLAs in policy to prefer low-latency pools, or 3) throttle background lanes.
- Postmortem: include decision traces and affected policy versions.

Open design questions / TODOs:
- Per-request credit accounting: how to bill correctly when a gold request executes on a low-cost pool? (ENG-PLAT-1428)
- Model-variant labeling and quality metadata schema: how to store fidelity/expected-delta per variant?
- Security: ensure cross-region spillover respects tenant isolation and encryption-at-rest policies for Private deployments.
- Autoscaling interplay: define a hysteresis model so autoscaling doesn't oscillate when spillover changes traffic shape.

Implementation notes / quick wins:
- Add 'lane' field to existing ingress token claims; default lane derived from plan.
- Extend control plane Decision API to include a 'fallback_hint' array of model ids to try in order.
- Small UI addition in Console: per-route lane config and a simple simulator button.

References and artifacts:
- See linked PR for prototype Decision API and a mock UI.
- Slack: channel platform-ops for real-time experiments.

Appendix: quick sample policy JSON (human readable)
{
  "route": "/v1/generate/chat",
  "policies": [
    {"lane":"gold","model_chain":["r-xl","r-xl-q8"],"max_latency_ms":120},
    {"lane":"silver","model_chain":["r-xl-q8","r-medium"],"max_latency_ms":250}
  ],
  "spillover": {"regionA":{"gold":["regionA-local","regionB-lowcost"]}}
}

Notes to reviewers:
- Looking for feedback on the lane taxonomy (should we add "partner" lane?), the size of the default model chains, and billing semantics during spillover.
- Prefer short, actionable changes to runtime for MVP: lane header + Decision API + lane-aware cache keys.

Last updated by Priya Desai on 2026-02-20.
